passages.text: Do not rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as to a father. Treat younger men as brothers, older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, with absolute purity.
passages.sermon:
Paul gives instructions to Timothy about how to treat people in the church.
Do not rebuke an older man.
Appeal to an older man as you would to a father.
Treat younger men as brothers.
Treat older women as mothers.
Treat younger women as sisters.
Always act with complete purity.
passages.original: Πρεσβυτέρῳ μὴ ἐπιπλήξῃς ἀλλὰ παρακάλει ὡς πατέρα νεωτέρους ὡς ἀδελφούς πρεσβυτέρας ὡς μητέρας νεωτέρας ὡς ἀδελφὰς ἐν πάσῃ ἁγνείᾳ

passages.text: Honor the widows who are truly widows.
passages.sermon: Honor widows who are truly in need.\r\nShow respect to women who have lost their husbands and have no one to care for them.\r\nGive special care to widows who are alone and have no family to help them.
passages.original: Χήρας τίμα τὰς ὄντως χήρας

passages.text: But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they must first learn to show godliness to their own family and repay their parents, for this is pleasing in the sight of God.
passages.sermon:
A widow may have children or grandchildren.
These children or grandchildren must learn to show godliness to their own family.
They must repay their parents.
God is pleased when they do this.
passages.original: εἰ δέ τις χήρα τέκνα ἢ ἔκγονα ἔχει μανθανέτωσαν πρῶτον τὸν ἴδιον οἶκον εὐσεβεῖν καὶ ἀμοιβὰς ἀποδιδόναι τοῖς προγόνοις τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ἀπόδεκτον ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: The widow who is truly in need and left all alone puts her hope in God and continues night and day in her petitions and prayers.
passages.sermon:
A true widow is a woman who is truly in need.
She is left all alone.
She puts her hope in God.
She continues to pray to God.
She asks God for help day and night.
She does not stop praying or asking God.
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ ὄντως χήρα καὶ μεμονωμένη ἤλπικεν ἐπὶ Θεὸν καὶ προσμένει ταῖς δεήσεσιν καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας

passages.text: But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive.
passages.sermon: A woman who lives for pleasure is spiritually dead.\r\nShe is still alive in her body.\r\nBut her spirit is dead.
passages.original: ἡ δὲ σπαταλῶσα ζῶσα τέθνηκεν

passages.text: Give these instructions to the believers, so that they will be above reproach.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy.
Paul gives Timothy instructions for the church.
Paul tells Timothy to command these things.
Paul wants the believers to obey these instructions.
Paul wants the believers to live above reproach.
passages.original: Καὶ ταῦτα παράγγελλε ἵνα ἀνεπίλημπτοι ὦσιν

passages.text: If anyone does not provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
passages.sermon:
A believer must care for his own family.
He must provide for his household.
If a person does not provide for his relatives, he denies the faith.
He is worse than an unbeliever.
passages.original: εἰ δέ τις τῶν ἰδίων καὶ μάλιστα οἰκείων οὐ προνοεῖ τὴν πίστιν ἤρνηται καὶ ἔστιν ἀπίστου χείρων

passages.text: A widow should be enrolled if she is at least sixty years old, the wife of one man, and well known for good deeds such as bringing up children, entertaining strangers, washing the feet of the saints, imparting relief to the afflicted, and devoting herself to every good work.
passages.sermon:
A widow may be enrolled if she meets certain requirements.
She must be at least sixty years old.
She must have been the wife of one man.
She must be well known for good deeds.
She must have brought up children.
She must have entertained strangers.
She must have washed the feet of the saints.
She must have helped those who are afflicted.
She must have devoted herself to every good work.
passages.original: Χήρα καταλεγέσθω μὴ ἔλαττον ἐτῶν ἑξήκοντα γεγονυῖα ἑνὸς ἀνδρὸς γυνή ἐν ἔργοις καλοῖς μαρτυρουμένη εἰ ἐτεκνοτρόφησεν εἰ ἐξενοδόχησεν εἰ ἁγίων πόδας ἔνιψεν εἰ θλιβομένοις ἐπήρκεσεν εἰ παντὶ ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ ἐπηκολούθησεν

passages.text: But refuse to enroll younger widows. For when their passions draw them away from Christ, they will want to marry, and thus will incur judgment because they are setting aside their first faith.
passages.sermon:
Paul gives instructions about widows in the church.
He says, do not enroll younger widows.
Younger widows may be led by their desires.
Their desires may draw them away from Christ.
They will want to marry.
By doing this, they set aside their first faith.
They will come under judgment for this.
passages.original: Νεωτέρας δὲ χήρας παραιτοῦ ὅταν γὰρ καταστρηνιάσωσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ γαμεῖν θέλουσιν ἔχουσαι κρίμα ὅτι τὴν πρώτην πίστιν ἠθέτησαν

passages.text: At the same time they will also learn to be idle, going from house to house and being not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, discussing things they should not mention.
passages.sermon:
Younger widows will learn to be idle.
They will go from house to house.
They will not only be idle.
They will also become gossips.
They will become busybodies.
They will talk about things they should not mention.
passages.original: ἅμα δὲ καὶ ἀργαὶ μανθάνουσιν περιερχόμεναι τὰς οἰκίας οὐ μόνον δὲ ἀργαὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ φλύαροι καὶ περίεργοι λαλοῦσαι τὰ μὴ δέοντα

passages.text: So I advise the younger widows to marry, have children, and manage their households, denying the adversary occasion for slander.
passages.sermon:
Paul gives advice to younger widows.
He tells them to marry.
He tells them to have children.
He tells them to manage their households.
He tells them not to give the adversary any reason to slander.
He wants them to live in a way that does not allow the enemy to accuse them.
passages.original: Βούλομαι οὖν νεωτέρας γαμεῖν τεκνογονεῖν οἰκοδεσποτεῖν μηδεμίαν ἀφορμὴν διδόναι τῷ ἀντικειμένῳ λοιδορίας χάριν

passages.text: For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.
passages.sermon: Some people have already turned away from the right path.\r\nThey now follow Satan.
passages.original: ἤδη γάρ τινες ἐξετράπησαν ὀπίσω τοῦ Σατανᾶ

passages.text: If any believing woman has dependent widows, she must assist them and not allow the church to be burdened, so that it can help the widows who are truly in need.
passages.sermon:
A believing woman may have widows who depend on her.
She must help these widows.
She must not let the church become burdened.
The church must remain able to help widows who are truly in need.
passages.original: Εἴ τις πιστὴ ἔχει χήρας ἐπαρκείτω αὐταῖς καὶ μὴ βαρείσθω ἡ ἐκκλησία ἵνα ταῖς ὄντως χήραις ἐπαρκέσῃ

passages.text: Elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
passages.sermon:
Elders lead the church.
Some elders lead well.
The church should give these elders double honor.
Some elders work hard at preaching.
Some elders work hard at teaching.
The church should especially honor elders who work hard at preaching and teaching.
passages.original: Οἱ καλῶς προεστῶτες πρεσβύτεροι διπλῆς τιμῆς ἀξιούσθωσαν μάλιστα οἱ κοπιῶντες ἐν λόγῳ καὶ διδασκαλίᾳ

passages.text: For the Scripture says, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain,” and, “The worker is worthy of his wages.”
passages.sermon: The Scripture gives instructions.\r\nThe Scripture says, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.”\r\nThe Scripture also says, “The worker is worthy of his wages.”
passages.original: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή Βοῦν ἀλοῶντα οὐ φιμώσεις καί Ἄξιος ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Do not entertain an accusation against an elder, except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
passages.sermon: An elder is a leader in the church.\r\nDo not accept an accusation against an elder.\r\nOnly accept an accusation if two or three witnesses support it.
passages.original: Κατὰ πρεσβυτέρου κατηγορίαν μὴ παραδέχου ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ ἐπὶ δύο ἢ τριῶν μαρτύρων

passages.text: But those who persist in sin should be rebuked in front of everyone, so that the others will stand in fear of sin.
passages.sermon:
Some people continue to sin.
You must rebuke these people.
Rebuke them in front of everyone.
This public rebuke will warn others.
Others will then fear sin.
passages.original: Τοὺς δὲ ἁμαρτάνοντας ἐνώπιον πάντων ἔλεγχε ἵνα καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ φόβον ἔχωσιν

passages.text: I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels to maintain these principles without bias, and to do nothing out of partiality.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy.
Paul gives a solemn command.
God is present.
Christ Jesus is present.
The chosen angels are present.
Paul commands Timothy to obey these instructions.
Timothy must not show favoritism.
Timothy must not act with prejudice.
Timothy must keep these principles fairly.
passages.original: Διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν ἀγγέλων ἵνα ταῦτα φυλάξῃς χωρὶς προκρίματος μηδὲν ποιῶν κατὰ πρόσκλισιν

passages.text: Do not be too quick in the laying on of hands and thereby share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul gives Timothy instructions for church leadership.
Paul says, “Do not be too quick to lay hands on anyone.”
Do not rush to appoint leaders.
If you do, you may share in the sins of others.
Do not join in the sins of others.
Keep yourself pure.
passages.original: Χεῖρας ταχέως μηδενὶ ἐπιτίθει μηδὲ κοινώνει ἁμαρτίαις ἀλλοτρίαις σεαυτὸν ἁγνὸν τήρει

passages.text: Stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead, because of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy.
Timothy is a young church leader.
Paul gives Timothy personal advice.
Paul says, “Do not drink only water.”
Paul says, “Use a little wine.”
Paul gives a reason.
Paul says, “You have stomach problems.”
Paul says, “You are often sick.”
Paul tells Timothy to use wine for his health.
passages.original: Μηκέτι ὑδροπότει ἀλλὰ οἴνῳ ὀλίγῳ χρῶ διὰ τὸν στόμαχον καὶ τὰς πυκνάς σου ἀσθενείας

passages.text: The sins of some men are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment; but the sins of others do not surface until later.
passages.sermon:
Some people sin openly.
Their sins are easy to see.
These sins go before them to judgment.
Other people sin in secret.
Their sins appear later.
passages.original: Τινῶν ἀνθρώπων αἱ ἁμαρτίαι πρόδηλοί εἰσιν προάγουσαι εἰς κρίσιν τισὶν δὲ καὶ ἐπακολουθοῦσιν

passages.text: In the same way, good deeds are obvious, and even the ones that are inconspicuous cannot remain hidden.
passages.sermon: Good deeds are easy to see.\r\nSome good deeds are not obvious.\r\nEven these hidden good deeds cannot stay secret.
passages.original: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὰ ἔργα τὰ καλὰ πρόδηλα καὶ τὰ ἄλλως ἔχοντα κρυβῆναι οὐ δύνανται
